why: The directive order is a preorder DFS that visits children in ascending index. In a preorder (Euler tour) array, every subtree is a contiguous block starting at its root, so the kth receiver from startNode is order[tin[startNode] + k - 1] whenever k <= subtree size.
hints: Write out the receive order from the root and from a child. How does the child's order sit inside the root's order?
Do one preorder DFS from person 1 with children sorted ascending. Record tin[v] (position in the order) and size[v]. The subtree of v is order[tin[v] : tin[v] + size[v]].

Each query is then O(1): return -1 if k > size[start], else order[tin[start] + k - 1]. Iterative DFS, O(n log n) for sorting children (already sorted if you build them by increasing index), O(n + q) after that.
pitfalls: Re-running a DFS per query is O(n * q), far too slow for 2 * 10^5 queries.
parent[i] describes person i + 1; persons are 1-indexed.
Children must be visited in ascending index order.
Recursion depth up to 10^5 crashes Python; use an explicit stack.
